title: Compact quant integration lab digest — Apr 04 2027
content:
Meeting: Compact Quant Integration — weekly research digest
Dates: 2027-04-04 (notes captured) / updated 2027-04-06
Attendees: Aisha, Marco, Sofia, Ethan, Priya (plus async comments from Jonas)
Context / objective:
- Triage and progress capture for the compact-precision onboarding stream: bring Sparc-13B and Sparrow-7B-lite through our quantization + runtime validation pipeline, with a focus on latency vs quality tradeoffs and KV cache memory footprint.
- Coordinate eval harness runs and regression gating for rollout to staging fleet.

Summary (high level):
- We finished baseline float32 and int8-static runs for Sparc-13B on a 2xA100 (timeout-friendly) instance. Preliminary evals show small perplexity delta (+1.8%) for int8-static but a 28% reduction in token cost. Latency at p50 is +6ms compared to float (networking noise excluded).
- Observed a KV-cache memory amplification on int8-per-channel mixed schemes for long-context (8k) traces — root cause likely memory layout changes in the kernel path.
- Microbatch tuning (microbatch size 2 -> 4) recovered missing throughput on dedicated infra for parity with float baseline under continuous batching.
- QA/eval pipeline: introduced an extra regression that measures answer-scoped BLEU/Rouge for our core assistant prompt set; flagged one prompt family with hallucination increase under 4-bit asymmetric quant.

Experiment log (concise run notes):
- run: sparc13b_float_baseline_0402
  - config: fp32, batch=1, seq_len=2048
  - infra: 2xA100-40GB
  - perf: p50=78ms, p90=120ms, tps=14.6
  - eval: perplexity=11.2, qa-f1=0.872
  - notes: baseline captured for comparison

- run: sparc13b_int8_static_0403
  - config: int8 static per-tensor, calibration on 10k samples, batch=1
  - infra: same
  - perf: p50=84ms (+6ms vs fp32), p90=132ms, tps=18.7 (batching improvements)
  - eval: perplexity=11.4 (+1.8%), qa-f1=0.865 (-0.8 pts)
  - cost: estimated token cost reduction ~28%
  - notes: acceptable quality for <30% cost reduction use-cases; submit for canary

- run: sparc13b_4bit_mixed_0404
  - config: layerwise 4-bit + per-channel scaling, dynamic activation quant during inference, microbatch=2
  - perf: p50=76ms (slightly faster), p90=118ms, tps=20.1
  - eval: perplexity=12.6 (+12%), qa-f1=0.834 (-4 pts)
  - notes: hallucination cluster on dialog-prompts -> must gate with reranking or fallback to fp32 for those prompt families

KV-cache memory anomaly (investigation notes):
- Symptoms: for long-context traces (~8k tokens) int8-per-channel runs consumed ~20–28% more host memory and showed increased GC/alloc churn in the runtime.
- Hypothesis: our custom kernel for per-channel scaling currently materializes an intermediate packed layout that duplicates KV shards until eviction occurs; float and int8-static paths avoid this.
- Quick repro: run long-context trace on dev box with DEBUG_KV_LAYOUT=1 and compare mallocs; reproduces consistently on both CUDA 11.8 and 12.1.
- Next steps: Marco to open a focused kernel-profiling PR, add allocation counters in the runtime, and produce a minimal repro. JIRA: JIRA-ML-3372 assigned.

Eval harness updates and gating rules:
- New eval: answer-scoped BLEU/Rouge added for assistant prompt set A (200 prompts), threshold: BLEU drop max 3 points, hallucination delta > 1.5x triggers automatic hold.
- Canary policy tweak: allow int8-static for internal dev tier with monitoring; require automatic fallback to fp32 for user-visible production routes where hallucination risk is high.
- Regression found: 4-bit mixed requires reranker enabled for certain RLHF-tuned prompts; plan: add explicit rerank tests to pre-merge checks.

Model onboarding status: Sparc-13B / Sparrow-7B-lite
- Sparc-13B: quantization pass in progress, int8-static canary ready, 4-bit mixed failing hallucination gate. Need to fix KV cache issue before staging rollout.
- Sparrow-7B-lite: lighter weight, 4-bit mixed looks promising (perf up, quality within 1.2%), will create dedicated canary route for mobile-optimized customers.

Operational notes / infra changes tried this week:
- Microbatching: adjusted microbatch size from 2->4 on sparc int8-static path to reduce per-token overhead; result: throughput improved 12–15% without pushing p90 beyond SLAs.
- Kernel selection heuristic: introduced a runtime flag to prefer int8-static kernels for short-sequence (<1024) requests to avoid per-channel memory path. Flag: FORCE_INT8_STATIC_SHORTSEQ (default false).
- Monitoring: added a KV-cache allocation gauge to Console (console PR queued) and an alert to SRE when per-request memory exceeds 3.5GB on 40GB cards.

Open questions / debates:
- When do we accept a small QA drop for cost savings? Proposal: product defines two accepted tiers (internal-dev: 5% QA drop allowed; production-customer: 1.5% max). Need product signoff — action for Priya.
- Should we enable per-channel quantization by default for new models? Tradeoffs: better per-layer accuracy vs memory churn and implementation complexity.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Marco Li: kernel allocation counters + minimal repro + PR (due 2027-04-09) — links to PR in linked_artifacts when ready.
- Sofia Nguyen: add rerank tests to pre-merge CI for RLHF prompt families (due 2027-04-08).
- Ethan Brooks: update canary rollout policy doc and create staging route for int8-static (due 2027-04-07).
- Priya Sharma: coordinate product decision on QA-drop-for-cost tiers; sync with Product-Hosted-API (meeting scheduled 2027-04-05).
- Aisha Patel: schedule deep dive on KV layout with runtime team and draft mitigation plan (due 2027-04-10).

Quick capture / notes-to-self (informal):
- "If we can limit per-channel path to long-context only, might be OK — avoid materializing in the hot path."
- Leave small exploratory set of 4-bit configs running overnight (Sparrow-7B-lite) and capture hallucination clusters by prompt id.
- Add one-off eval that runs with reranker disabled to measure worst-case hallucination.

References & useful links:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rv-serve/pull/1892 (microbatch change + short-seq flag)
- JIRA: JIRA-ML-3372 (KV-cache memory investigation)
- Confluence: confluence://applied-ml/compact-quant-integration (design notes and calibration scripts)

Next sync: weekly standup + deep-dive on kernel allocation (2027-04-11, 10:00 PST).
